problem: The formula box gives R = H( H(h1 || h2) || H(h3 || h4) ), which is only the four-leaf case, but it appears inside the general build section that starts with n transactions. A student can read it as the general definition.
fix: Label it: for n = 4, R = H( H(h1 || h2) || H(h3 || h4) ); in general, keep pairing and hashing level by level until one hash is left, and that hash is R.

problem: The note says H is 'SHA-256 in Bitcoin'. Bitcoin's Merkle tree applies SHA-256 twice: the leaves are txids = SHA-256(SHA-256(tx)) and each internal node is SHA-256(SHA-256(left || right)). Stating only SHA-256 is imprecise.
fix: Say H is double SHA-256 (SHA-256 applied twice, SHA-256d) in Bitcoin, so the leaf of transaction Ti is hi = SHA-256(SHA-256(Ti)) and an internal node is SHA-256(SHA-256(left || right)). The root is still 32 bytes.
